name: pulse_widths
about: Three pulse trains of the same shape and three different widths, sampled at 50 ms so the narrowest is one tick wide. Five pulses of 50 ms at 5% duty, then five of 100 ms at 10%, then five of 300 ms at 30%, each cycle exactly one second so a pulse never straddles two slow ticks. The question this asks is not whether the ladder mitigates - it is what the slow cadence can see at all. The ladder moves on a one-second window and needs rise_ticks of it, so a pulse narrower than that window is averaged into it rather than seen, and the duty cycle rather than the peak is what reaches the engine. Read the detect_ticks and missed_pulses columns together: a train that is entirely missed at 5% and answered at 30% locates the floor of what this cadence can respond to.

timeline.note: one second of quiet before the first train
three seconds of quiet, long enough for the descent to complete
